title: Personal Sin
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Personal sin means that every person sins in thought, desire, word, action, and failure to do what is right. Sin is personal rebellion against God, not merely weakness, mistake, or social brokenness.
summary: Personal sin means that every person sins in thought, desire, word, action, and failure to do what is right. Sin is personal rebellion against God, not merely weakness, mistake, or social brokenness.
christFocus: Jesus Christ came to save sinners from real guilt and personal sin. He bore sins in His body on the cross so those who believe may be forgiven, cleansed, and made new.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Every person sins personally before God. Sin includes wrong actions, corrupt desires, false words, unbelief, pride, lust, hatred, and failure to do the good God commands. No one is innocent by personal record.

Personal sin is ultimately against God. Sin may harm others and damage the sinner, but its deepest offense is rebellion against the holy Lord. David confessed that his sin was against God, even though it also wounded people.

Scripture does not allow people to hide behind comparison. All have sinned and fall short of God’s glory. Denying sin only deepens deception, but confession opens the way to mercy.

Christ came because personal sin is real. He did not die for vague human imperfection, but for sinners who need forgiveness, cleansing, reconciliation, and new life.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often minimize sin by calling it personality, struggle, mistake, trauma response, addiction, or weakness. Those realities may help explain pain, but they do not erase moral responsibility before God.

This doctrine gives a path to honest grace. If sin is denied, forgiveness is avoided. If sin is confessed, Christ is shown to be the Savior who cleanses real guilt and restores real sinners.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Name your sin honestly before God without excuses or despair. Confess thoughts, desires, words, actions, and neglected obedience. Receive Christ’s forgiveness by faith, make restitution where needed, and walk in the light with repentance and hope.
